units.note: ἐφ᾽ ὅσον ... ἐπὶ τοσοῦτον correctly rendered.
πέντε δὲ καὶ δέκα μυριάδας = 150,000, correct.

findings.quote: Then, when he made his entrance into the senate
findings.problem: The Greek has a gap (***) immediately before 'τότε δὲ κατὰ τὴν εἴσοδον γενόμενος τὴν εἰς τὴν σύγκλητον'; the English opens with 'Then' as if the text were continuous. The lacuna is silently smoothed.
findings.proposed_fix: [...] Then, when he made his entrance into the senate

units.note: Lacuna marker only; no text invented.

findings.quote: Because they were generally displeased by visits from kings, they issued a decree
findings.problem: 'ὡς γὰρ καθόλου δυσαρεστούμενοι ταῖς τῶν βασιλέων ἐπιδημίαις δόγμα τι τοιοῦτον ἐξέβαλον': ὡς + participle gives the senate's alleged ground (as though displeased in general), a pretext cloaking its particular hostility to Eumenes, not a stated real cause. English turns it into a flat 'because'.
findings.proposed_fix: On the pretext of a general displeasure at visits from kings, they issued a decree

findings.quote: the senate dealt with all who had arrived on embassies
findings.problem: Greek 'λοιπὸν ἡ σύγκλητος ἅπασιν τοῖς παραγεγονόσι κατὰ πρεσβείαν:' has no governing verb (colon follows directly); a verb has dropped out or the text is defective. English supplies 'dealt with' without marking it.
findings.proposed_fix: the senate [verb missing in the Greek; sense presumably 'gave audience to'] all who had arrived on embassies

units.note: Second finding is a probable gap/ellipsis in the transmitted text; do not resolve beyond a bracketed mark.
